end.summary:
Practised timelines: BCE dates count backwards; CE dates go to the right.
Discussed archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions as historical sources.
Aarav named pottery, bones, and coins as archaeological evidence.
Aarav continued to treat books or inscriptions as complete and fully reliable sources; this was not corrected after the last attempt.
Teach-back was not passed.
end.parentNote: Asha practised placing BCE and CE on a timeline and identifying archaeological remains, inscriptions, texts, and oral traditions. Aarav gave examples such as pots, bones, and coins; they also mixed up the idea that a written source must be completely true, and this was not corrected after the last attempt. At home, ask Aarav to sort examples into four source groups and explain why historians compare more than one source.
